description:
A benchmark can be enforced in code (registered in cross_surface.GATES) yet not
pinned in the Make/CI surface - the standardized-command test does not assert that
every gate has a corresponding *-cross-surface-equivalence-report Make target and
a pr.yml correctness-gate step. The newer gates (ClickBench, JoinOrder-synthetic,
H2O-DB) are exposed to exactly this drift: enforced in GATES, but their
Make/CI pinning is maintained by hand and can fall out of sync.

Add a check that DERIVES the expected Make targets and pr.yml steps from the live
GATES registry and fails when a gate lacks its target or CI step. This closes the
same drift class as the mutation-target guard (set(_TARGETS)==set(GATES)), one
layer up at the Make/CI boundary.

anti_patterns.dont: hand-maintain a second list of expected gate names
anti_patterns.why: derive from GATES, or the guard itself drifts.

preserves.behavior: No change to gate behavior; this is a drift guard over the Make/CI surface.

prior_art.concept: {'ref': '.github/workflows/pr.yml:404', 'note': 'The per-gate correctness-gate steps (ssb/amplab/coffeeshop/clickbench/joinorder/h2odb) that must be derivable from GATES.'}
{'ref': 'benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py (GATES)', 'note': 'The single source of truth the check derives from.'}

{'ref': 'tests/integration/test_cross_surface_mutation_sensitivity.py:332', 'note': 'test_targets_cover_every_enforced_gate is the precedent: assert a registry-derived set equals the live GATES set. Mirror it for Make/CI targets.'}

{'ref': 'tests/unit/test_standardized_test_commands.py', 'note': 'Existing standardized-command test; extend it (or add a sibling) to derive expectations from GATES rather than a hand-maintained list.'}

verifications.description: Adding a gate without its target/step fails the guard
verifications.expected: passes for current GATES; fails if a GATES entry lacks a Make target or pr.yml correctness-gate step

work_units.notes:
Add a test that, for each name in cross_surface.GATES, asserts a
`<name>-cross-surface-equivalence-report` Make target exists AND a
corresponding step is present in pr.yml's correctness-gate job. Parse the
Makefile and pr.yml as text/data; key off GATES so adding a gate without its
target/step fails. Account for the name normalization already used
(joinorder_synthetic -> joinorder-synthetic-...).
work_units.summary: Assert every GATES entry has a Make target and a pr.yml correctness-gate step
